The senator representing Ondo North Senatorial District, Jide Ipinsagba, has called on members of the All Progressives Congress to put aside their differences and embrace unity ahead of the 2027 general elections, particularly the re-election of President Bola Tinubu. Ipinsagba made the appeal in a statement issued on Thursday following a court victory that affirmed his position as the APC’s senatorial candidate for Ondo North. The Federal High Court in Abuja had on Tuesday struck out a suit filed by a party aspirant and former member of the House of Representatives, Gbenga Elegbeleye, challenging Ipinsagba’s candidacy. The ruling leaves Ipinsagba as the recognised APC flagbearer for the senatorial district ahead of the 2027 elections. In the statement, the senator thanked party stakeholders for their support, describing the court outcome as an opportunity for reflection and renewed commitment to his mandate. The statement read, “I give all glory and gratitude to Almighty God for the victory recorded today in the pre-election court case. The outcome is a moment of appreciation, reflection and renewed commitment to the mandate and responsibility entrusted to me. “Now that this chapter has been addressed, I warmly appeal to you to join hands with me as we work together to strengthen our party, promote unity and advance the collective interests of our people. NANS hails FG over planned passport production centre 2027: Lagos APC warns members against internal divisions City Boy executives back Gombe director “There is more that unites us than divides us and the future of our party and district must take precedence over individual differences, ahead of the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and other APC candidates.” Ipinsagba commended the Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, and other party leaders for their support, while urging Elegbeleye to join efforts to reconcile members and strengthen the party ahead of the forthcoming election. “To my brother and fellow contestant Gbenga Elegbeleye, I commend your decision to pursue your grievances through the court rather than abandon our great party. “Your choice to choose judicial redress reflects the democratic process and the importance of resolving political differences within the framework of the law,” the senator lauded. The APC is expected to intensify efforts to consolidate its support base ahead of the 2027 general elections, with party leaders calling for unity among members following internal disputes over candidates and leadership positions. Tinubu, who won the 2023 presidential election, is seeking a second term in office, while the party is also working to retain its seats in the National Assembly and state legislatures. In Ondo State, Ipinsagba’s court victory is expected to strengthen his position as the party’s candidate in Ondo North, although reconciliation with aggrieved aspirants remains important to the APC’s efforts to present a united front in the district.
